Biotechnol"},"printPublicationDate":"2027-08-01"},"pubYear":"2027","abstractText":"Microbial cell factories have emerged as important platforms for the sustainable production of fuels, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and other value-added bioproducts. Synthetic biology provides a systematic engineering framework for their construction and optimization through standardized biological parts, modular design, and iterative Design-Build-Test-Learn cycles. This chapter summarizes the major tools and strategies for developing microbial cell factories, beginning with the fundamental principles of synthetic biology and the characteristics of representative microbial chassis. Key genetic engineering approaches, including CRISPR-based genome editing, transcriptional and translational regulation, and modular DNA assembly, are discussed together with strategies for metabolic pathway design, enzyme engineering, flux balancing, and dynamic regulation. Genome-scale metabolic modeling, adaptive and directed evolution, and multi-omics analysis are further introduced as systems-level approaches for identifying engineering targets and improving cellular performance. In addition, emerging computational tools, machine learning, artificial intelligence, high-throughput screening, and laboratory automation are highlighted for their roles in accelerating strain development and closing the Design-Build-Test-Learn cycle. regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) and associated (Cas) systems have revolutionized the field of genome engineering by providing versatile, efficient, and programmable tools for precise genetic manipulation. Originally identified as an adaptive immune mechanism in prokaryotes, CRISPR/Cas systems have been extensively repurposed for a wide range of applications across molecular biology, biotechnology, and medicine. This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms underlying CRISPR/Cas immunity. Furthermore, the classification of CRISPR/Cas systems into distinct types and subtypes is discussed, highlighting their structural and functional diversity. Advances in genome editing technologies, including CRISPR-mediated knockout, base editing, and prime editing, are explored with an emphasis on their mechanisms and applications. The chapter also examines emerging CRISPR-based platforms for transcriptional regulation, epigenome editing, and RNA targeting, which enable precise and reversible modulation of gene expression without altering genomic DNA. In addition, the transformative impact of CRISPR technologies on functional genomics is addressed, particularly through high-throughput screening approaches that facilitate the identification of gene function and genetic vulnerabilities. CRISPR-based diagnostic tools and therapeutic strategies are also reviewed, underscoring their potential in disease detection and treatment. Despite significant progress, challenges such as off-target effects, delivery limitations, and safety concerns remain critical considerations. Overall, this chapter highlights the expanding capabilities of CRISPR/Cas systems and their growing importance in both fundamental research and clinical applications.","affiliation":"Izmir programmable manipulation of the genome and epigenome. This chapter provides a comprehensive and practical guide to genetic and epigenetic editing using CRISPR technology, with a particular focus on applications in Ewing sarcoma cell models. We describe strategies for CRISPR-mediated gene knockout (CRISPR KO) via nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ), precise gene knock-in (CRISPR KI) through homology-directed repair (HDR), and reversible transcriptional modulation using CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) and CRISPR activation (CRISPRa). We emphasize the use of ribonucleoprotein (RNP) delivery of Cas9 and single guide RNAs, which offers improved editing efficiency, reduced off-target activity, and enhanced safety compared to plasmid-based approaches. Detailed protocols are provided for guide RNA design, RNP assembly, electroporation-based delivery, single-cell cloning, and molecular validation of edited clones. In addition, we outline best practices for HDR template design, discuss strategies to improve KI efficiency, and address common challenges such as polyploidy, variable editing rates, and DNA-mediated cytotoxicity. For CRISPRi and CRISPRa applications, we describe plasmid-based systems employing catalytically inactive Cas9 fused to transcriptional repressors or activators, enabling potentially tunable and reversible control of endogenous gene expression. Throughout the chapter, practical advice, troubleshooting tips, and critical considerations are included to facilitate successful implementation across diverse experimental settings. Collectively, this chapter serves as a detailed methodological resource for researchers aiming to employ CRISPR-based engineering for functional studies.","affiliation":"Hopp Children's Cancer Center
